releases.name: OpenCode plugin 0.1.8
releases.body:
OpenCode plugin **0.1.8** refreshes the model catalog and carries two Claude Code releases' worth of stability work (0.1.6 and 0.1.7) that OpenCode users have not had yet: a code-health pass over the review, write and state code, and fixes for Windows and macOS.

**What's new since 0.1.4**

- **Model catalog:** Claude Fable 5.2 replaces 5.1, Gemini 4 Carbon replaces Gemini 4 Argon, codex gains `gpt-6.1-terra`, kimi leads with `kimi-k3.1-pro`, and kilocode adds `kimi-k3.1-pro`, `hy4`, `nex-n2.6` and Meta's Muse Wonder through OpenRouter. The retired `arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking` row is gone, and the free OpenCode default moves from `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` to `opencode/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-free`.
- **Fewer failed or stuck rounds:** odd or malformed model output no longer crashes a round; a damaged checkpoint or status file is set aside and the run continues; `--reaggregate` records HIGH findings and finishes only whole rounds.
- **Safer writes and rollback:** every phase that writes files holds its folders until its last write, rollback copies come from a vetted file handle, and a killed run's leftovers are cleaned up. `--output-format json` prints one JSON document on the apply phases.
- **Provider handling:** an OpenCode slot that loops on empty steps is stopped, kilocode errors and rate limits are classified from its own error lines, and a plan outside any git repository can run native apply.
- **Windows and macOS:** abort sends Ctrl+Break only to a console group the plugin made, copies are never written through a link planted at their name, and a moved folder is named on macOS too.
- **Host runbooks:** the OpenCode package writes the whole runbook to a file the host can read.

**Needs action:** the base `providers.yaml` changed, so re-run `--init --force` in each project to pick up the new defaults. If you keep your own model lists, replace `claude-fable-5-1`, `gemini-4-argon`, `kimi-k3`, `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` and `arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking`. No config keys were renamed or removed. One fallback changed: a provider with no configured row now gets a 1,200 s timeout instead of 600 s.

Set the exact plugin pin in your OpenCode config and restart while online:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-multi-llm@0.1.8"] }
```

Tested host: **OpenCode 1.19.5 on Linux** (the minimum and the latest release). macOS and Windows remain untested on the npm installation route. Keep the other entries and settings in your existing config. Users switching from the file-command route should run `uninstall-host opencode` first, so the old file command does not duplicate the npm plugin's.

**Verification**

Immutable tag source: `c36cf4cccb91f3318f6d76c3b7d7d1fff2c88681`, the same commit as Claude Code 0.1.8 and Codex 0.1.8 (shared-payload digest `b7d25d18…`).

- All four required PR checks passed on that exact commit: Ubuntu, macOS, Windows and `package`.
- The full serial suite passed: 36,485 tests.
- The full local OpenCode gate passed rows 1–9 and 5b on OpenCode 1.19.5, including the five installed-package container scenarios. Package digest: `21ef7c9673e1a28d6543c9d5c93846397ed323f407fe0bafdd5418a9e567f743`.

The published package passed all nine registry install criteria in a clean container on OpenCode 1.19.5, including cold dependency install, warm offline operation, a same-pin restart, and a real 0.1.4 → 0.1.8 upgrade that ran the new payload. Registry integrity:

```text
sha512-HCQy6MOP/X8T8oguVs1AD8js3OahK2DdhYh1ZDlImCV3RE+NgM/A8wErzC84yHxfW48pSfB00ue4eIpoFQev/g==
```

Accepted npm provenance identifies certified publishing source `537a49e9ec55970c86d04b540499ce93c30a6e5b` on `refs/heads/master`, repository `beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin`, workflow `.github/workflows/publish-opencode-plugin.yml`. Its rebuilt package digest exactly equals the independently gated tag: `21ef7c9673e1a28d6543c9d5c93846397ed323f407fe0bafdd5418a9e567f743`. Publish: [successful OIDC workflow](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/

- **Fewer failed or stuck rounds:** odd or malformed model output no longer crashes a round; a damaged checkpoint or status file is set aside and the run continues; `--reaggregate` records HIGH findings and finishes only whole rounds.
- **Safer writes and rollback:** every phase that writes files holds its folders until its last write, rollback copies come from a vetted file handle, and a killed run's leftovers are cleaned up. `--output-format json` prints one JSON document on the apply phases.
- **Provider handling:** an OpenCode slot that loops on empty steps is stopped, kilocode errors and rate limits are classified from its own error lines, and a plan outside any git repository can run native apply.
- **Windows and macOS:** abort sends Ctrl+Break only to a console group the plugin made, copies are never written through a link planted at their name, and a moved folder is named on macOS too.
- **Host runbooks:** Codex now reads the whole runbook in bounded pages it can confirm.

If you keep your own model lists, replace `claude-fable-5-1`, `gemini-4-argon`, `kimi-k3`, `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` and `arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking`. No config keys were renamed or removed, and the minimum Codex stays 0.159.2. One fallback changed: a provider with no configured row now gets a 1,200 s timeout instead of 600 s.

Upgrade an existing marketplace installation:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade beastlabai
codex plugin add multi-llm@beastlabai
```

For a new installation, first add the marketplace:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin --ref release \
  --sparse .agents --sparse packaging/codex
codex plugin add multi-llm@beastlabai
```

Start a new Codex session. Existing project provider configuration stays in place. Tag-pinned users should select `codex-v0.1.8`.

**Verification**

Verified source: `c36cf4cccb91f3318f6d76c3b7d7d1fff2c88681`, the same commit as Claude Code 0.1.8 and OpenCode 0.1.8 (shared-payload digest `b7d25d18…`).

- All four required PR checks passed on that exact commit: Ubuntu, macOS, Windows and `package`.
- The full serial suite passed: 36,485 tests.
- The full local Codex gate passed 17 rows on Codex 0.167.0 (pinned), 10 rows on the minimum 0.159.2 and 10 rows on the latest, 0.167.2, with no `features` diff. The upstream validator is absent; repository layout rules and actual Codex ingestion passed.

Fresh public tag and promoted-release installs passed all six criteria on Codex 0.167.2 in a stock container, with all 327 files matching the tag. A real public-release 0.1.4 → 0.1.8 marketplace upgrade ran the new MCP payload, and a same-version refresh kept its bytes. No paid model requests were used.

Evidence: attached canonical `20261112T153934Z-codex-release-network-check.json` (also committed under `skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/`) and sanitized `codex-public-verification.json`. Promotion: [successful workflow](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/actions/runs/43251051718).

releases.name: OpenCode plugin 0.1.4
releases.body:
OpenCode plugin **0.1.4** ships the latest master changes: explicit scope policy across review, validation, application and resume, plus visible scope tags in Markdown and HTML review reports.

Set the exact plugin pin in your OpenCode config and restart while online:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-multi-llm@0.1.4"] }
```

Tested host: **OpenCode 1.19.5 on Linux**. macOS and Windows remain untested on the npm installation route. Keep the other entries and settings in your existing config. Project `.multi-llm/providers.yaml` stays in place; this release needs no provider-config migration. Users switching from the file-command route should remove the old file command before enabling the npm plugin to avoid duplicate commands.

All nine canonical fresh-registry criteria passed: exact package integrity and tree, manifest version, installed command, actual payload execution, cold dependency installation, offline operation with network cut, same-pin restart, and a real **0.1.3 → 0.1.4** upgrade executing the new payload. No paid model requests were used.

Immutable tag source: `89fea1893ec332fc5462c5b95ee712404a898d32`. Accepted npm provenance identifies certified publishing source `8d605c9b9d74ba6b4580081838296126212d8802` on `refs/heads/master`, repository `beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin`, workflow `.github/workflows/publish-opencode-plugin.yml`. Its rebuilt package digest exactly equals the independently gated tag: `bcdf5f4fb5f402dad25402603e49497180050acdd1d07f59ba6ea5a51d5ca905`.

Registry integrity:

```text
sha512-qajLxl8eSG2qzkmwEDYgW301/xd4rN+CPq59Al3STbc0cjtH1A5rtY69S3sVr9NC07EBi0FEV762zsDrjDYqcQ==
```

All four required PR and master CI checks and both local/tag release gates passed. Publish: [successful OIDC workflow](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/actions/runs/41278049174).

Attached evidence: `20261101T004126Z-opencode-release-gate.json`, `20261101T061412Z-opencode-release-network-check.json` (also committed under `skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/`), `certified-source-equivalence.json`, and `npm-provenance-verification.json`.

releases.name: OpenCode plugin 0.1.3
releases.body:
The OpenCode Multi-LLM plugin now includes the current master runtime, including commit-range review and guarded fix workflows, sharper review prompts, and detached-log fixes. Shared version: 0.1.3.

Requires OpenCode 1.19.5 or newer and uv on PATH. Change your exact plugin pin and restart OpenCode:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-multi-llm@0.1.3"] }
```

Confirm it loaded with `opencode debug config` and check that `command["multi-llm"]` exists. Existing provider configuration is preserved. File-route users should first run `uninstall-host opencode` from their original installation to remove its command shim.

The full local gate passed rows 1–9 and 5b on OpenCode 1.19.5, including all five installed-package container scenarios. Release source: `c9ae61b027a9e7bac4db216353495077f9c1d6f2`. [Committed gate record](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261030T155243Z-opencode-release-gate.json). The publisher preserves GitHub-certified source metadata and requires its rebuilt package digest to equal the independently gated release tag. The dispatch-source rebuild at `cfe445b4543b733b9754df807f1e7c224fb15de7` matches that digest exactly. The OIDC publication succeeded with npm 11.5.1 and Node 22.23.4. Its accepted provenance identifies the correct repository, `.github/workflows/publish-opencode-plugin.yml`, and certified dispatch source `cfe445b4543b733b9754df807f1e7c224fb15de7`; the published subject digest matches the registry package. [Publishing run](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/actions/runs/41129206642).

A fresh stock-container install passed all nine later-release criteria, including exact installed-tree equality with the tag, first-use dependencies, offline operation with the network cut, restart, and an actual upgrade from 0.1.1 executing the new payload. [Committed registry install/upgrade proof](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261030T214755Z-opencode-release-network-check.json).

Integrity: `sha512-b4rfpMp/eLCeYMx506jEyRbCIXzgfg9DKChejXIyxHAFMDUZH/01Jw4wWkHiOLdqNDojfV08K16/gaybJQxpYg==`.

The gate record, registry proof, source-equivalence proof, and provenance verification are attached. Raw supporting logs remain local because they contain machine-specific paths. All package and install checks used local stubs; no paid model calls were made.
